releases.notes: Container images and a gateway mode: unmask.sh/admin and unmask.sh/nginx (the official nginx image with the module) are served from unmask.sh like the packages, mirrored on GHCR; with UNMASK_UPSTREAM set the nginx container terminates TLS, so JA4 works, and proxies what passes to any HTTP server. Settings > Gateway manages the vhost name and certificate (Let's Encrypt via nginx's ACME module, a pasted purchased certificate, or files) and shows what :443 serves. Fixed: the setup wizard dead-ended when the token existed only at the legacy path; the live tail dropped and reconnected every minute behind a vhost-level proxy_read_timeout. The live tail now shows flag, network, user agent and path; doctor warns when an install's history has split across host ids; the bot-hunt date column is back to 13rem.

Two security fixes. The challenge page could redirect a visitor off-site through ?_test_redirect= — a URL parser strips TAB/CR/LF before parsing, defeating the old character checks — on every install with default settings; and alert mail could have a header injected through a notification subject. Also: doctor no longer claims a packaged challenge asset is being served, unpinning a popover no longer strands it, and the bot-hunt date cell no longer paints over the IP beside it.

The bot-hunt timeline shows which TLS fingerprint each phase actually presented (a beacon is its own connection). Every unset axis action now resolves to pow_then_captcha, so the funnel separates cannot-run-JS from headless solver from person. The absence of a verdict is one token everywhere, (none), and the statistics tables' user-agent columns read like the hunt log's. Rebind lineages are kept 15 days, past both cookie defaults.

Security: a proof-of-work cookie no longer satisfies a bot-verdict JA4 rule on either wire — seen live with a residential-proxy herd; native installs need render-nginx and a reload. A bot-verdict fingerprint with no chain inherits the operating default through one resolver, closing a forward-auth challenge loop. The stats range picker goes below a day (1h/3h/6h/12h).

Security: a headless browser could clear the behavioural CAPTCHA at full marks — the check now reads how movement was built, not just its shape — and the numeric-add fallback no longer hands CAPTCHA grade to scripts. The hub feeds are signed (ed25519) and range updates work offline. Bypass presets follow the user-agent policy you already set. Notifications gain a visible tab, pausable channels, an explicit mail_to list and __hostname__ labels; admin accounts can be disabled and invited by a setup link with no password ever mailed. The over-block breaker counts browser-grade traffic only.

A CAPTCHA pass is a pass, not proof of a person: the overview separates solves from returning cookie traffic. Truncation popovers work on Firefox. A geo or ASN rule's chain is now the chain that gets served on native installs, and the embedded challenge assets are authoritative — a custom page needs the explicit challenge_html_path / challenge_js_path setting.

Security: a geo or ASN rule set to a CAPTCHA was satisfied by a proof-of-work cookie; both modes now fold the network axes into the grade requirement. An ASN rule matching on organisation rendered a config nginx refused to load (unquoted space). The bot-hunt log orders a session by when the browser sent each beacon, honeypot bans name the probed host, and the built-in CAPTCHA is the recommended one.

Anthropic's crawlers are verified by their published IP ranges (new claude preset, on by default for fresh installs). unmask stats dumps the numbers without opening the database. The over-block breaker no longer trips on a scanner farm, the traffic-composition card shows its breakdown honestly, and a hunt row names its Host when it cannot be inferred.

A fresh forward-auth install on nginx locked you out of its own admin: the protected rule never reached the challenge, which served a proof-of-work screen the gate then refused, forever. A challenge is now never served that the gate would refuse. Collapsing a bot-hunt session keeps its badges.

Security: the community feed enforced nothing on forward-auth deployments — Apache and stock nginx never read the map files. The daemon now enforces in-process from the same bytes, a hit is reported as its own axis, its action is yours to pick (default captcha_only), and a PoW-only install no longer loops on it. Retention pruning runs in bounded batches so it cannot starve the ban lookup.

Security: a protected path ending in a CAPTCHA was satisfied by a proof-of-work cookie, on the product's own admin login; both modes now require CAPTCHA grade there. A protected path's mode is the challenge it runs (pow / captcha / pow_then_captcha, the new default; strict is gone). Raw-event retention defaults to 7 days for fresh installs, and the retention tab projects the disk.

Upgrade review: on the review policy (default for fresh installs) a new default-on enforcement preset stays inert until you acknowledge it; rescue presets are never held. Shipped presets are active from the release that ships them, replacing the drifting seen_version gate. A GCP load-balancer health-check stats-exclude preset.

The admin-host allowlist speaks in hosts: exact, subdomain, or regex — 'contains' would have admitted example.com.attacker.com — and rejects a pattern it cannot use instead of saving short under a green banner. A rejected rule-list save keeps what you typed. Each settings tab has its own URL.

Security: a rule whose chain ends in a CAPTCHA is satisfied only by a CAPTCHA-grade pass; each solve records its grade into the credential, and a re-bind checks the lineage's grade. Re-bound passes are reported as their own kind rather than as CAPTCHA solves, monitoring-mode cookies never count as solves, and the overview reads the hourly rollup instead of scanning the event log.

A schema migration could wedge an install forever when the database already carried part of its work. The abandonment rate no longer counts rule-targeted crawlers. Rendering unchanged settings leaves the files alone, and doctor notices a rendered config nginx never loaded. Publishing verifies what is actually served, and unmask version names its commit.

Security: 'deny' did not deny — every axis except the ban was consulted only when the visitor held no pass cookie, so a crawler that solved the proof of work rode through a deny rule for a week. A resolved deny is now enforced beside the ban on both wires. A pre-release channel for confirming fixes, and the overview no longer counts requests twice.
A visitor who left while the challenge page was holding lost the solve they had already made; the wait now happens after the cookie is written.

Lowering the proof-of-work difficulty now warns that it breaks the site until nginx reloads. The challenge page's presentation is a setting (min_display_ms, invisible_reveal_ms). The rate-limit funnel rollup no longer wedges on a verdict-less event, and challenge_targets.all is gone in favour of the Operating-mode buckets.

Every visitor was held 1.5 seconds before the challenge let them through, entirely artificially: PoW p50 1508ms to 389ms. Browsers without TextEncoder no longer loop forever. A pattern can declare how it is read (regex / contains / exact), bypassed requests are counted apart from people, and hunt says why a challenge fired.

The dashboard says what a site's traffic is made of, in requests. Bot hunt ranks the networks traffic came from, not just addresses. The proof of work runs in a Web Worker so background tabs are not throttled to a minute. unmask drops to the daemon's user when run as root, and a visitor with no User-Agent is no longer classified as unmask's own fetcher.

The default rate limit is three parallel axes: per-IP, per-JA4 and per-IP+JA4, each with its own threshold. Admin login and password reset throttle in the application, where the nginx preset never fired. Every settings value list renders as confirmed rows with an off switch and a note, rate-limit zones enforce identically on both wires, and the hunt log tells apps, browsers and bot kinds apart.

Crawlers that publish their egress ranges are verified by address rather than by name, as standing policy on by default. Apple push-notification previews pass behind a TLS-fingerprint guard. Hunt paging survives the log's own growth, a support ref lookup drops from 53 seconds to 9ms, and the site-scoped challenge preview moved under /unmask/test/.

SQLite memory is budgeted for the whole daemon instead of per connection, so unmask fits on a 1GB VPS (3.7GB peak to 447MB on the same benchmark). A Performance tab shows the resource dials for this host. The header-integrity axis no longer charges pre-2021 browsers for a header they never had.

A per-site setting no longer freezes everything else about that site. The header-integrity axis is on by default. The audit log records where each action came from, the cookie-reuse ranking covers PoW cookies, and you can see visitors who gave up on the challenge — and whether they went back or left. Chatwork and other Japanese link-preview bots pass out of the box.

The header-integrity axis works behind a TLS-terminating load balancer, where it had silently never fired. unmask warns when a reload cannot apply what you changed because nginx is still running on replaced libraries — a state where fresh workers can die with SIGSEGV.

Block or challenge traffic by network (ASN), not just by country, evaluated after the bypass-IP check so search crawlers are never caught. Throttle a network or country instead of blocking it. Verify a claimed crawler by reverse DNS. Challenge a Chromium browser missing its client-hint header (opt-in). doctor warns when config.yml was hand-edited without re-rendering.

Both deploy modes share one daemon upstream, unmask_daemon — forward-auth installs with an edited server.inc must move to the new name. FHS cleanup for immutable /usr. Saving settings no longer deletes config sections owned by other programs, and the forward-auth endpoint no longer rebuilds its matchers on every request.

The admin tells you when the daemon cannot write its own database, the classic silent-stats failure. Per-site challenge logos actually work and live under /var/lib/unmask. The test pages can exercise a specific site's challenge end-to-end.

The UA-filter checkbox and the Bypass-IP range presets are independent axes, with a live badge showing each crawler's true rescue path. Saving a settings tab no longer silently rewrites settings you did not touch — a no-op-save test flushed out the geo tab's save that had never worked. The stale-browser tier follows an unmask.sh feed and covers Firefox.

Security: a spoofed crawler User-Agent no longer walks through the challenge — during the 2026-07-15 incident a 94k-IP botnet was waved through on a fake Googlebot string. Range-publishing vendors are rescued by IP. A browser pinned to an outdated Chrome can be escalated to a CAPTCHA (off by default), and the dashboard is dramatically faster on large installs.

Compose mode leaked every challenged connection, exhausting nginx's fd budget and taking the node down within hours; all three native production nodes went down this way. Fixed with an explicit finalize on the internal redirect.

Security: on AlmaLinux / RHEL 8 the nginx plugin read the wrong request fields, and compose-mode protected locations let every bot through. On SELinux hosts without semanage native mode recorded zero events, and every restart rewrote challengeable honeypot bans as hard deny. The admin no longer redirect-loops when the CSRF cookie expires, and the stats pages no longer slow as events accumulate (unmask db-analyze).
A stats-exclude 'private networks' preset, structured rows for IP and host lists, and doctor probes :80 as a load-balancer health checker.
Configurable HTTPS-redirect exemptions with ACME and load-balancer health-check presets on by default — an un-exempted 301 drops the node from the LB. A preview-language selector on the theme tab.
An HTTP to HTTPS redirect option (off by default), bypass-path presets with per-preset factory defaults, and a fix for the access-log parser dropping fields on TLS-resumption lines.

Privacy Pass verification and Web Bot Auth behind an Advanced switch. A support Ref ID on every challenge page with a reverse lookup, a branded deny page in 18 languages, native rate-limit deny mode, IPv6 /64 binding for the _bv cookie, a q-prefix JA4 for HTTP/3, Apache JA4 capture at parity with nginx, an in-app update check, and a broad hardening pass across authentication, input handling and the challenge primitives. Dropped Caddy and Traefik as shipped integrations.
First public release of unmask.
